scientific_question: Do donors with worse memory decline have a higher fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons that are both exposed to nearby reactive astrocytes and locally depleted of neighboring pyramidal neurons?
rationale: Rounds 1-5 established a strong CA1 reactive-astrocyte niche signal, but the last addition produced only a very small gain, which suggests the current panel is nearing saturation on astrocyte-only summaries. The next focused test should ask whether the same niche also carries a distinct neuronal disorganization signal: pyramidal neurons sitting in reactive-astro neighborhoods while lacking nearby pyramidal peers. That is mechanistically interpretable as reactive-astro-associated local pyramidal dropout or isolation, and it could add nonredundant signal or serve as a cleaner replacement for a weaker astro-only member.
approach: Assign cells to CA1 using CustomAnnotations polygons after dividing annotation coordinates by 16. From ClassificationNode labels, select CA1 Pyramidal Neuron and Reactive Astrocyte centroids. For each CA1 pyramidal neuron, count (1) reactive astrocytes within a 30 um radius and (2) other CA1 pyramidal neurons within the same 30 um radius, excluding the index cell. Mark a pyramidal neuron as 'reactive-astro-associated isolated' if it has at least one reactive astrocyte neighbor and no more than k other pyramidal neighbors. The donor-level biomarker is the fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons meeting that criterion.

variations.name: candidate_variant_a
variations.description: Fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons with at least 1 reactive astrocyte within 30 um and at most 5 other CA1 pyramidal neighbors within 30 um.

variations.name: candidate_variant_b
variations.description: Same feature, but the low-pyramidal-neighbor threshold is relaxed to at most 8 other CA1 pyramidal neighbors within 30 um.

notes: Use centroids only; no contour-derived morphology is needed. Keep the radius at the same 30 um scale as prior accepted niche features, converting microns to pixels with slide MPP if available from the paired SVS; in this cohort 30 um is about 60 px. Exclude the index pyramidal neuron from the pyramidal-neighbor count. If CA1 is missing or a donor has zero CA1 pyramidal neurons, return NaN gracefully.
prompt_text:
# Candidate Proposer

You are proposing exactly one candidate biomarker round for an iterative
autoresearch loop.

This system is deliberately simple:

- there is one accepted biomarker panel so far
- each round proposes one new candidate biomarker family
- the worker may test a small local sweep within that candidate family
- the evaluator compares:
  - current accepted panel score
  - panel + candidate score
  - panel with one member replaced by the candidate
- the system then keeps the best reviewed panel only if it improves the train panel score

Your job is only to propose the next candidate.

You will receive a JSON payload containing:

- `program`: the research directive
- `data_summary`: dataset guide
- `accepted_panel`: the current accepted biomarker panel
- `recent_results`: recent keep/discard history from results.tsv
- `round_id`
- `candidate_type`: `seed` if the panel is empty, otherwise `candidate`

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "short stable slug",
  "scientific_question": "one sentence stating the candidate hypothesis",
  "rationale": "why this candidate is the right next test based on recent results",
  "approach": "how to compute the biomarker from the data",
  "variations": [
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_a",
      "description": "baseline or central parameterization"
    },
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_b",
      "description": "one nearby local change"
    }
  ],
  "baseline_variation": "candidate_variant_a",
  "notes": "data access, coordinate, or implementation notes for the worker"
}
```

## Rules

- Propose exactly one candidate family per round.
- Keep the candidate biologically interpretable.
- If `candidate_type` is `seed`, propose the strongest plausible seed biomarker.
- If `candidate_type` is `candidate`, propose something that could improve the
  accepted panel either by adding new signal or by being a cleaner replacement
  for one weaker existing member.
- Prefer one local family sweep with 2-4 nearby variations, not a grab bag of
  unrelated ideas.
- Use recent results to avoid exact repetition.
- Make the local sweep explicit and small:
  - one radius change
  - one threshold change
  - one local operator change
  - or one biologically coherent gating change
- Do not talk about planners, branches, coordinators, or analyzers.
- Focus on one candidate that is easy to compute and easy to audit.

## Quality bar

A good proposal is:

- specific
- testable in one round
- mechanistically interpretable
- plausibly additive to the accepted panel
- not a vague restatement of the prior winner
